Would you like to default to one mode in particular the next time you turn on Rufus? Not a problem; mf(x) has built in memory that remembers your last mode choice. sources.bodyExcerpt: Suhr Announces The Rufus Reloaded Fuzz: A Deep Technical and Pedagogical Analysis for Guitarists | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / practice tips practice tips Suhr Announces The Rufus Reloaded Fuzz: A Deep Technical and Pedagogical Analysis for Guitarists By Zoe Langford July 11, 2026 Suhr Guitars has officially launched the Rufus Reloaded Fuzz — a meticulously re-engineered iteration of their acclaimed 2017 Rufus Fuzz pedal. Unlike superficial cosmetic updates, this version features a redesigned transistor biasing network, expanded dynamic headroom (+3.2 dB at unity gain), recalibrated tone stack with ±12 dB shelving response at 800 Hz, and an all-new low-noise JFET input buffer. Measured THD at 1 kHz is 0.0018% in clean bypass mode, dropping to 0.0024% when engaged but buffered — a 17% improvement over the original. Built on a 4-layer FR-4 PCB with gold-plated through-hole components and a CNC-machined aluminum enclosure (118 mm × 68 mm × 52 mm), the pedal ships with a custom 9V DC power supply delivering ultra-low ripple ( Historical Context and Design Philosophy The original Rufus Fuzz debuted in 2017 as Suhr’s first standalone stompbox — developed in close collaboration with guitarist and clinician Rufus Lee. Its design prioritized touch sensitivity, organic decay characteristics, and amp-like compression behavior rather than high-gain saturation. Early units used hand-selected 2N5088 transistors with h FE ranges tightly binned between 220–245, resulting in subtle unit-to-unit variance. While beloved by players like John Mayer and Robben Ford, users reported two consistent limitations: inconsistent low-end response below 120 Hz and diminished note separation during rapid alternate picking passages above 140 BPM. Suhr’s engineering team spent 27 months addressing these issues — conducting spectral analysis on over 1,200 recorded guitar phrases across five amplifier platforms (including a 1965 Fender Bassman reissue, a 1973 Marshall JMP Super Lead, and a modern Two-Rock Custom Shop Signature). Their findings confirmed that the original’s 1st-order high-pass filter at the input stage (cutoff at 142 Hz) was truncating fundamental resonance in drop-D and open-G tunings. Additionally, the output stage’s emitter follower configuration introduced slight phase inversion artifacts during fast transients, degrading transient clarity. From Lab to Lineage The Rufus Reloaded incorporates three foundational upgrades rooted in empirical measurement: First, a dual-stage active high-pass filter now sets the cutoff at 72 Hz ±3 Hz — verified via swept sine testing using Audio Precision APx555 instrumentation. Second, the output buffer employs a complementary pair of ON Semiconductor MMBT3904/3906 transistors, eliminating phase inversion and reducing group delay from 8.7 μs to 2.3 μs. Third, the bias network now uses a temperature-compensated voltage divider with 0.1% metal-film resistors (Vishay CMF55 series), ensuring stable operating points across ambient temperatures from −10°C to +45°C. Circuit Architecture and Signal Path Breakdown Understanding the Rufus Reloaded’s internal topology is essential for intentional use — especially in educational settings where students must correlate knob adjustments with audible outcomes. The signal path flows through six discrete stages: (1) JFET input buffer (Toshiba 2SK372), (2) active high-pass filter (72 Hz), (3) dual-transistor gain stage (2N5088 ×2, h FE 235–250), (4) passive tone stack (Baxandall-derived, center frequency 800 Hz), (5) soft-clipping diode network (1N914 ×4 arranged in parallel-series configuration), and (6) compensated emitter-follower output. This architecture departs significantly from classic fuzz topologies. Rufus is a unique pedal that offers a vast array of fuzz tones. Whether your tastes are for the historic tones created at The Fillmore East back in ‘69, or you crave the more aggressive, mid-scoped characteristics of the Grunge-era, Rufus has you covered, and then some. Also includes a foot-swichable and extremely tactile octave-up effect. We focused our development on creating a powerful, easy to play octave-up, that responds evenly across all of your instrument’s pickup selections and the entire fingerboard – effortlessly delivering the iconic “Band of Gypsys” tone at your fingertips. Beyond Traditional Designed for ultimate versatility, Rufus is equipped with a full featured 3-Band EQ that gives you the ability to easily shape Rufus’ tone without compromising the sound of your guitar or bass rig. Did we just say bass? Yes we did. Rufus is an equal opportunity fuzz pedal that plays well with guitars and basses – no need to worry about losing your bottom-end here. One Pedal, Two Modes Created to enhance your overall playing experience, we developed Multi-Function Technology mf(x). mf(x) is a proprietary foot switch technology that enables you to seamlessly select between Rufus’ two distinct user modes, Normal and Octave, during a performance just by holding down it’s foot switch. Would you like to default to one mode in particular the next time you turn on Rufus? Not a problem; mf(x)has built in memory that remembers your last mode choice. Advanced Features True Bypass: Rufus Reloaded is true bypass via a relay. This function allows for the remote switching, and the battery monitor feature. The relay produces less popping when switching the pedal on and off. FX Link: The FX Link connector allows the pedal’s switching function to be controlled from an external switch, pedal board, loop switcher, or any other custom interface. FX Link also provides the ability to power up in the On/Off state. Low Battery Monitor: Rufus Reloaded incorporates a unique battery monitor that alerts the user to low battery conditions. In addition, the battery monitor will automatically switch the pedal to True Bypass if the battery voltage is too low for the circuitry to correctly operate. sources.bodyExcerpt: Bilmuri x Tallon Electric - The Hog Skip to content Home Products Contact About Search More Home Products Contact About More Search Account Cart 0 The Hog Wield the tone of BILMURI 126 reviews Kinda Hard Motorsports The Hog Nighthog Edition $189.00 ADD TO CART THE HOG employs a dangerous blend of distortion and overdrive to produce tones that are THICC and CRYSTAL CLEAR . CONTROLS: + CRANK: Controls the gain of the distortion tone OPTIMIZE: Blends between the distortion tone (ccw) and the crunch tone (cw) LOAD: Sets the total output volume CLARITY: Cuts or boosts the overall brightness BEEF: Set upward for ultimate lows, or downward for a tighter bass response SECRET SWITCH: Open your pedal to find a secret setting! The Hog was tailored for use with single coil pickups. Slide this switch to the right when using higher output pickups to clean up your crunch tone. TECH SPECS: + POWER SUPPLY NOT INCLUDED . It's definitely full, and fattens up the sound much more than just the dirt channel on my Marshall. I mostly play pop-punk rhythms, but it handles drop-A on a 7-string just fine without bottoming out. I still haven't figured out how to get the exact Bilmuri snappy sound yet, but I also don't play a Strat. There's plenty I haven't figured out with this pedal, but that's the best part. 5/5 for fit, finish, and overall experience. Will be buying from Tallon again! Privacy Terms Accessibility Back to Products EL CAMBO OVERDRIVE Classic Tube Overdrive Pedal with Intuitive 3-Knob Interface for Essential Blues Rock Tones 1 / 4 Zoom View in fullscreen EL CAMBO OVERDRIVE Classic Tube Overdrive Pedal with Intuitive 3-Knob Interface for Essential Blues Rock Tones Share Overview Learning Features Downloads About this product Classic Tube Overdrive Pedal with Intuitive 3-Knob Interface for Essential Blues Rock Tones EL CAMBO OVERDRIVE As far as versatile and ubiquitous effects go, an overdrive emulating a pushed tube amp is as good as it gets. EL CAMBO fattens up your tone with a little (or a lot) of extra girth around the waist, providing that highly sought-after midrange “oomph” that cuts through the mix, especially when your band is pushing hard decibels. This particular gritty honk gives your guitar a powerful voice that is ideal for a singing blues solo, and it’s also perfect for a hard rockin’ lead boost over the top of your amp’s already overdriven sound. Crank it up and testify! • Vintage all-analog overdrive • True Bypass • Built like a tank A Mountain of Mids EL CAMBO OVERDRIVE delivers a distinct midrange boost, one that can instantly warm up your tone, even if it’s a bit too jangly to cut through a loud rhythm section. Thanks to its symmetrical clipping overdrive circuit, the harmonic saturation is amazingly fluid and musical sounding. Boost into Epic Solo-Mode With plenty of gain and boost on tap, EL CAMBO can be tailored to work in almost any setting. From adding just a bit of push to your preamp with subtle warmth to your tone, to a screaming overdrive with singing sustain and thickness, EL CAMBO gets you there. Whether the moment calls for blistering Texas-style blues, soulful pop ballads or classic rock riffs – EL CAMBO fits the bill! Roadworthy Made from a sturdy metal housing, this all-analog overdrive will last for years and years without losing that warm tube saturation tone. EL CAMBO’s top-mounted jacks help save pedal board space and corral your cables, while the true bypass operation keeps your signal nice and clean.

Privacy Terms Accessibility Back to Products EYEMASTER METAL DISTORTION Skull-Pounding Metal Distortion Pedal with 2-Knob Interface for Insane Gain 1 / 4 Zoom View in fullscreen EYEMASTER METAL DISTORTION Skull-Pounding Metal Distortion Pedal with 2-Knob Interface for Insane Gain Share Overview Learning Features Downloads About this product Skull-Pounding Metal Distortion Pedal with 2-Knob Interface for Insane Gain EYEMASTER METAL DISTORTION EYEMASTER METAL DISTORTION brings back the original metal credo of "loud and brutal" with its "simpler-than thou" 2-knob operation.Just set the volume (all the way up, right?) and adjust the gain (anything less than all-the-gain is sacrilege) and start riffing.EYEMASTER was specifically designed to channel the Swedish death metal tone, endearingly nicknamed the "Swedish buzzsaw". As that term implies, EYEMASTER is not a subtle overdrive.It is not transparent and it does not "sit well in a mix". Rather, it burns an unholy path straight through the mix. • Aggressive death metal distortion • All-analog circuitry • True Bypass All. The. Gain. The concept of gain is something we often take for granted, and rarely do we stop to think about what the term actually means. In many ways, gain has been given a bad name; mankind has been tricked into believing such blatant nonsense as “less is more”, and other sophomoric terms like “transparent” or “authentic” are better. EYEMASTER brings back elemental, primordial gain – the kind of raw gain by which empires are either built or shattered! Perfect EQ Stop wasting time on EQs. We’ve already dialed-in the perfect death metal EQ and cut off the knobs. Just turn the remaining knobs all the way up and unleash your inner beast with an authentic death metal sound that is evocative of ancient pagan rituals performed in the depths of the Scandinavian woods. Tones that are dark and menacing – and dripping with acid and edge. Forged from Unholy Metal With its sturdy and strong metal frame, EYEMASTER will stand up to an army of black clad metal players and keep asking for more. Dead simple 2-knob operation and top-mounted jacks provide an easy fit on your pedal board, and the true bypass keeps your signal nice and clean. (Hey, you’ve gotta tune sometime, right?)

sources.description: The TC Electronic Eyemaster Metal Distortion is a high-gain distortion pedal designed for brutal metal tones, particularly the "Swedish buzzsaw" sound. With a simple 2-knob interface for easy control of volume and gain, it delivers extreme saturation and in-your-face distortion. Built with a rugged chassis and true bypass, the Eyemaster is built to deliver consistent sound and performance on any pedalboard, channeling the spirit of Swedish death metal.

sources.description: The TC Electronic FANGS METAL DISTORTION is a high-gain distortion pedal designed for metal and heavy rock guitarists. It offers ultra-thick distortion tones, a versatile mid control, and a super-tight response, making it ideal for both rhythm and lead playing. With its three distinct modes, including Raw, Fat, and Scoop settings, guitarists can dial in a variety of metal tones from classic thrash to modern scooped sounds. The Fangs Metal Distortion features true bypass, top-mounted jacks for pedalboard convenience, and a rugged enclosure, making it a road-ready choice for metal enthusiasts. The pedal delivers all the gain needed, and is an affordable choice for guitarists.

Privacy Terms Accessibility Back to Products GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION Organic Tube-Like Distortion with Tight Bottom-End and Natural Sag 1 / 4 Zoom View in fullscreen GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION Organic Tube-Like Distortion with Tight Bottom-End and Natural Sag Share Overview Learning Features Downloads About this product Organic Tube-Like Distortion with Tight Bottom-End and Natural Sag GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION Overflowing with organic tube amplifier-like distortion, tube compression and tight bottom-end tone, GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION channels the very essence of rock ‘n’ roll. Couple all that tone with the sultry feel of a vintage tube-rectified power supply and endorphin-elevating affordability – and you’ve got a shiny one-way trip to guitar Nirvana! Raw Rock Power Nothing has shaped the musical landscape more than a roaring tube guitar amp set to 11 – that incredible sound remains the heart and soul of rock. GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION distills the heavenly, rich harmonic content and power supply sag that made those early tube amps the “Holy Grail” for scores of guitar-wielding legends. So if your riffs call for tight bottom-end, rich mids and creamy highs, GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION stands ready to deliver. 50+ Shades of Gain GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION isn’t just a one-trick tone pony; its ultra-wide gain range and smooth tonal character, mixed with super-tight low-end response, lets you go from a Hendrix-style crunch to beefy Blackmore distortion – and all the way to super-saturated solo tones in a flash. Whether your gig calls for dark vintage distortion, or an extra-crispy modern high-gain tone, you’ll find it here in the super-versatile GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION. Classic Tone – Modern Features We know that the battle for a place on your pedalboard is fierce, so we equipped GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION exceptionally well to make the cut. A sturdy metal chassis with dedicated Input, Output and True Bypass means that GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION is equally roadworthy and pedalboard friendly. You can power it with a 9V battery, or use our convenient POWERPLUG 9V adapter. Your pedalboard will welcome GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION with open arms! Backstage Pass – All Access Capable of a tremendous range of classic tube amp tones, GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION sports an easy-to-use control layout including: Gain, which controls the amount of overdrive; Volume, controls the output level; and Tone, for setting the sound for anywhere between dark, old-school dirty to crisp and modern distortion. Nothing is easier!Check out GRAND MAGUS DISTORTION at your local TC ELECTRONIC dealer today, or get yours online – and turn your tone up to eleven!

It's just begging for a loud tube amp to really open up and breathe.The range of gain available in Honeypot Fuzz goes from a slightly gritty grind, almost like an overdrive, and all the way to massive walls of sticky honeycomb-structured distortion with seemingly endless sustain and a tone that's fat and nasty but with thick,sweet highs.Honeypot covers a wide musical territory that spans all the way from The Black Keys and The White Stripes to 90's alternative rock all the way up to the Dark Side Of The Moon with a beautiful creamy and vibrant sustain. • Vintage style fuzz pedal • All-analog circuitry • True Bypass Classic Fuzz Tones HONEY POT FUZZ faithfully delivers the instantly recognizable distortion guitar sound found on iconic rock albums from the ‘70s onward. sources.bodyExcerpt: TC Electronic HONEY POT FUZZ Fuzz Pedal with Sustain Review: The Sweetest Path to a Massive Wall of Sound – SonicMetric Skip to content Home Gear Reviews Best Guides Pro Insights Contact us Search Toggle Menu Search Gear Reviews TC Electronic HONEY POT FUZZ Fuzz Pedal with Sustain Review: The Sweetest Path to a Massive Wall of Sound By NotahEuthymia February 6, 2026 As guitarists, we’ve all been there: you’re trying to replicate that massive, soaring lead from a classic Pink Floyd record or the crushing, thick rhythm of a 90s alternative rock anthem, but your current setup feels thin. You crank the gain on your amp, and it just gets fizzy. You try a standard distortion pedal, and it lacks the “soul” and harmonic complexity you crave. This is the common struggle of finding a fuzz that provides both girth and smoothness without becoming a chaotic mess of noise. Solving this “thin tone” problem is crucial because, without the right saturation, your solos lack sustain and your riffs lack the authority to command a stage. The complication is that many boutique fuzz pedals are prohibitively expensive or too temperamental for a standard pedalboard. That is where our journey with the TC Electronic HONEY POT FUZZ Fuzz Pedal with Sustain began—a search for a vintage-flavored solution that doesn’t break the bank. TC Electronic HONEY POT FUZZ Vintage-Flavored Fuzz Pedal with Massive Wall of Tones and Miles of... Heavy sounding fuzz pedal with massive wall of tones Dial in massive amounts of gain that makes the angels sing See latest price What to Consider Before Buying Guitar Distortion Overdrive Effects A Guitar Distortion Overdrive Effects is more than just an item; it’s a key solution for shaping the emotional resonance of your music and defining your signature sound. Whether you are playing in a bedroom or a stadium, these pedals act as the bridge between your fingers and the listener’s ears, providing the texture, sustain, and grit necessary for modern music styles. When we evaluated the TC Electronic HONEY POT FUZZ Fuzz Pedal with Sustain , we looked at it through the lens of how well it solves the problem of “sonic emptiness” by filling the frequency spectrum with rich, even-order harmonics. The ideal customer for this type of product is someone facing the limitation of a “dry” amplifier sound or a lead guitarist who needs notes to ring out for days. It is perfect for fans of the Big Muff-style circuit who want something more rugged and affordable. However, it might not be suitable for those who prefer the transparent, “edge-of-breakup” sound of a Klon-style overdrive or players who need extreme surgical precision in their high-end frequencies without any “hair” on the notes. For those players, a specialized boost or a transparent overdrive might be a better fit. Before investing, consider these crucial points in detail: Dimensions Space: In the world of modern pedalboards, real estate is at a premium. You need to consider if the pedal uses top-mounted or side-mounted jacks, as this significantly affects how many units you can cram onto a board. We found that while the TC Electronic HONEY POT FUZZ Fuzz Pedal with Sustain is robust, its footprint is a consideration for those with crowded setups. Capacity/Performance: Look for the “Gain Range.” A great fuzz should be able to go from a light, “fuzzy” overdrive to a full-blown wall of noise. The sustain capacity is also vital; you want a pedal that allows a note to bloom and hold its pitch without dying out prematurely into static. Materials Durability: Guitar pedals live a hard life on the floor, being stomped on by boots. A “Built-like-a-tank” metal chassis is non-negotiable for touring musicians. Privacy Terms Accessibility Back to Products MAGUS PRO Classic High Gain Distortion Pedal with Fat Mids, Treble Filter Control and 3 Clipping Modes 1 / 6 Zoom View in fullscreen MAGUS PRO Classic High Gain Distortion Pedal with Fat Mids, Treble Filter Control and 3 Clipping Modes Share Overview Learning Features Downloads About this product Classic High Gain Distortion Pedal with Fat Mids, Treble Filter Control and 3 Clipping Modes Versatile Classic Analog Distortion If you’ve ever needed a Classic Analog High Gain Distortion Pedal but been unable to find one with enough versatility to suit any scenario, the MAGUS PRO will be a very welcome surprise for you. Its slow slew rate, treble filter control and three different modes of operation provide more than enough variance in approach and tone to compliment any playing style. Slow Slew Circuitry We’ve specially designed a circuit to recreate the classic slow slew of the infamous LM308 op-amp using readily available modern components. By keeping the slew rate slow, harsh unwanted harmonic overtones and interference are eliminated, leaving you with a smooth layer of pure distortion whilst cranking the gain. Filter That Treble to Your Needs One particularly distinctive feature of the MAGUS PRO is the Treble Filter control. It’s an extremely effective Hi-cut filter, allowing you to totally tailor your top end bite. Three for the Price of One! MAGUS PRO comes packed with three different modes, giving you more scope than ever before. CLASSIC MODE takes us to a world of oldskool, high gain, punchy MIDS and a gripping tight bottom end. TURBO MODE meanwhile engages LED clipping diodes for greater headroom, less saturation and higher output level. Finally, FAT MODE gives the low end a boost while re-shaping the upper MIDS for that ultimate hard rock tone. Warm Sustain for Days When you punch in the MAGUS PRO as a solo boost, evenly balanced harmonic resonance produces effortless and lasting sustain to take you way over the horizon. It’ll also provide musical feedback when required at high gain settings, whilst its slow slew rate keeps unwanted sizzle at bay. All of this is delivered with a warmth and tone that you’d expect from only the finest analog circuitry. True Bypass True bypass ensures you keep a totally pure signal and retain the integrity of your instrument’s tone when the pedal is not in use. Tough and Compact MAGUS PRO is housed in an amazingly compact, built-like-a-tank metal box. Ever conscious that your pedal collection may be growing while your pedalboard may not, we’ve mounted the jack sockets and power input on the top of the housing to save you valuable pedalboard real estate. Allowing you to stack more pedals than ever before in a row.

It goes like this: a guitarist with a four-decade career, a signature Ibanez, a wall of Marshalls and access to literally any overdrive ever built gets asked which pedal matters most to him. He names one that costs less than a set of strings and a decent lunch. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO That is the TC Electronic MojoMojo Overdrive, and the guitarist is Paul Gilbert. Speaking to Guitarist magazine in 2016 — an ordinary interview, not a promo video, not a launch campaign — Gilbert was asked about pedals and gave one of the more honest answers in the genre. He described his ideal pedal as a “placebo box” that does nothing but makes you feel like you’re playing better. Then he named the actual one. “As far as specific pedals, the one that’s really been a mainstay is the TC Electronic MojoMojo,” he said. “It’s really a normal [overdrive] pedal. There’s nothing unusual about it except it just sounds good.” Nothing unusual about it except it just sounds good. If you had to compress the entire appeal of this pedal into ten words, that would be the ten. And it is the reason the MojoMojo, fifteen years after launch, is still in production, still in the top few hundred distortion pedals at Europe’s largest music retailer, and still selling for less than fifty dollars — a price that has caused more confusion about its quality than any review ever could. This is the story of a genuinely great cheap overdrive, the enormous artist roster attached to it (most of which does not survive scrutiny), and the one name on that roster that survives beautifully. How to Get the Tone ↓ Where the MojoMojo Came From: The Noise People Get Into Dirt TC Electronic was founded in 1976 in Denmark by brothers Kim and John Rishøj. As Premier Guitar ‘s Matthew Holliman put it in the pedal’s launch review, they were self-described “experts on noise” who set out to clean up a guitar world full of crackling, popping effects. Their breakthrough was the SCF Stereo Chorus Flanger, which won over guitarists and keyboard players largely because it was quiet — a competitive advantage that sounds trivially boring today and was anything but in 1980. Features: Special modified MOJOMOJO overdrive pedal designed in collaboration with Paul Gilbert Voice switch replaced with extra gain mod, this one goes to eleven! Increased circuit board voltage gives dramatically more headroom and dynamics for an incredibly alive overdrive sound 4-knob interface enables extensive tonal tweaking while remaining highly intuitive to let you focus on playing 2-band EQ with active bass and treble knobs lets you really shape your sound True bypass allows for optimum clarity and zero signal loss when the pedal is off Easy one-screw battery compartment access Compact format fits on any pedal board High-quality components to give you extraordinary overdrive tones Sturdy die-cast metal case designed for life on the road Tone Up with Paul Gilbert We’re very excited to have collaborated with the mighty Paul Gilbert on a specially modified edition of the MOJOMOJO OVERDRIVE pedal. If you’re looking for a huge overdrive sound, you better ally with Mr. Big himself to have the fundamental tone dialed in just right! Sporting a couple of tweaks to the circuit and a stylish new purple Jacket, MOJOMOJO PAUL GILBERT EDITION is like the perfect chicken tender, combining juicy and crunchy in the most delicious way possible! But This One Goes to Eleven Paul always uses his original MOJOMOJO pedal with the same voice setting, so we swapped out the Voice switch for a new 11 switch. Flipping the 11 switch engages a massive gain boost for even more drive and attack. And believe us, this one really does go to 11 in that totally meaningful and wildly rocking Spinal Tap-like fashion, giving you that last push over the cliff! Warning! High Voltage Territory Ahead We added stepped-up circuit board voltage to the MOJOMOJO PAUL GILBERT EDITION, giving you dramatically increased headroom and dynamics for an incredibly alive and soaring overdrive, keeping your tone crisp – but not toasted! sources.description: My TC Electronic Nova Drive Review - the Nova Drive uses analogue circuitry for tone with digital for control and patches, packing two different analogue distortion effects (overdrive and distortion) in one relatively small stompbox. This isn’t overdrive or distortion either – it’s both, with each having its own separate “engine”, so both can be used together.
sources.snippet: TC Electronic Nova Drive Review | Guitar Pick Zone
sources.bodyExcerpt: TC Electronic Nova Drive Review | Guitar Pick Zone Skip to content About Me Privacy Policy Contact Me Cookies Guitar Pick Reviews Guitar Gear Reviews Menu Toggle Amplifiers Pedals Accessories Electric Acoustic Bass Search for: Search Search Main Menu Guitar Pick Reviews Guitar Gear Reviews Menu Toggle Amplifiers Pedals Accessories Electric Acoustic Bass TC Electronic Nova Drive Review NDR-1 By Justin / October 14, 2018 Last Updated on November 27, 2022 by Justin Mention the words ‘digital’ and ‘distortion’ together to your average guitarist and he’ll likely shout abuse as he hits you – justifiably so too. This is because while digital circuitry works very well for certain types of effects, only analog can deliver the tone that we like for our distortion effects. Digital has some great advantages though – programmability and flexibility. For example, many delays and chorus effects as well as modulation in general. Is becoming increasingly popular. It allows us to store patches as well as control things from other digital devices. Usually, these two worlds do not meet, and we end up compromising either tone or control, depending on our preferences. The ambitious concept behind the Nova Drive is analog circuitry for tone, digital for control and patches, packing two different analog distortion effects (overdrive and distortion) in one relatively small stompbox. This isn’t overdrive or distortion either – it’s both, with each having its own separate “engine”, so both can be used together. What’s more, you can route the two in series or parallel and in any order and then save all the settings to any of the 18 patches. First Impressions Of The Nova Drive The first impressions are good – it is an attractive pedal with a solid feel. The weight is a hefty 0.8 kg, thanks to the solidly made, neatly finished black metal enclosure. The knobs are rubber with clear position markers and the pots and switches are bolted to the chassis and have a solid feel when used. Connections Connection is fairly simple, with input and output jacks, a DC power input, and a MIDI input for external control. There is also an external switch jack for the TC Electronic G-Switch, which adds a further three footswitches for additional foot control. It is worth noting that there is no battery compartment as the Nova Drive uses 380 mA of 12V DC power – which is out of the range of battery power (and is more than some commonly used pedalboard power units can supply). Thankfully, a wall-wart power supply is included. Using The TC Electronics Nova Drive Compared to most common overdrive or distortion pedals, the Nova Drive is fairly complex. However TC Electronic has done a great job of making it simple to use – for the most part, it operates like two pedals in one housing. Most of the controls are familiar and even those that are not (such as the patch functions, switch modes, and routing) are easy to figure out. The only time I needed to refer to the manual was to figure out how to change the bypass modes. How Does The Nova Drive Sound? Sound is important. That goes without saying. So let’s take a look at how this pedal really sounds. Overdrive The overdrive is a smooth, natural overdrive with a very usable but simple tone control, good dynamics, and a good range of drive on tap. The drive range goes from clean boost to heavy overdrive but doesn’t quite make it into modern metal territory, even with humbuckers. It is very responsive to playing dynamics and volume changes so you can leave it cranked and use the guitar’s volume control to set the drive. There is a slight upper midrange emphasis which stops it from being a perfectly transparent clean boost, but not too excessive, just a subtle and usable ‘push’ to the sound. A final and unique feature is the ability to mix in the bypassed sound with the overdriven to add more clarity to the tone. Distortion The distortion is capable of everything from slightly crunchy to classic metal tones – all without any hint

sources.bodyExcerpt: Dual Distortion - TC Electronic Vintage Pedals Home Pedals Dual Distortion Overdrive Compressor Octa Screamer Tube Primer Distortion Delay Bass Distortion Tremolo About Contact TC Electronic Vintage Pedals Vintage Dual Distortion General Technical Pictures < > Archived Manufacturer Information Description The Vintage Dual Distortion is a distortion pedal for all times. The full-bodied vintage sound is pleasantly warm and crispy, and adds solidness to the bottom that spurs memories of the past. Switch between the two gain settings and enjoy the power and the mood of dual distortion. With the color filter knob you can get that extra edge to the top end, while keeping the original sound intact. Satisfy your longing for vintage distortion. Main Features Gain A Level – Sets the amount of distortion on channel A. Gain B Level – Sets the amount of distortion on channel B. Output Level – Sets the overall output level. Color Filter – This tone control adds or subtracts the high end frequencies of your signal allowing you to match the driven signal with the bypassed. Press GAIN A or GAIN B to activate the respective channels, automatically deselecting the opposite channel. Opamp 2x ​ OP07DP Controls ​ Gain A Level, Gain B Level, Output Level, Color Filter ​ Connections 1/4 inch input jack, 1/4 inch output jack, DC jack 2mm (centerpin is negative) ​ ​ Power Supply ​ 9-12 Vol DC or battery 9V Alkaline. Effect Usage ​ 20mA ​ Dimensions ​ 100mm x 120mm x 50mm Input 1/4” connection Output ​ 1/4” connection Equivalent T-Rex Pedal "Dr. Swamp" V1 Powered by Create your own unique website with customizable templates. With the additional boost section, top and mid boost, remote control, and a vintage-type speaker simulation, VPD1 is a genuinely versatile guitar pedal. Our scientists designed the VPD1 to reproduce warm driven vintage tones that you would normally only get from a tube amp with the master volume turned all the way up. Simplicity, great sound, and timeless design make up the holy trinity of the VPD1 vintage pre-drive pedal. This pedal is all about bringing out the best in your favorite guitar/amp setup without any unwanted coloring of tone or quality-compromising add-ons. VPD1 would therefore serve as an excellent companion for the G-System from TC Electronic. The basic drive section delivers a distinguished vintage overdrive allowing every characteristic of your instrument to shine through. When you kick in the boost section, you get a saturated lead sound with plenty of gain and sustain. Additional features on the boost section are the Top and Mid boost emphasis filters that let your tone really cut through. VPD1 features a unique circuit, which accurately replicates every group of components in an original vintage tube amp combo, including the dynamic interaction that occurs between the components. In addition to the drive functionality, VPD1 actually serves as a small preamp, ranging sonically from barely audible overdrive to snarling leads - and beyond. In the VPD1 signal path, the boost section is placed before the drive, which means that the boosted guitar signal not only sounds louder but also sounds more overdriven. This makes it ideal for switching from rhythm to lead guitar. The remote function even allows you to switch the VPD1 boost on and off with the new G-System from TC Electronic, or any other external relay switching device. For your convenience, we've also included top and mid boost switches for a more flexible sonic exploitation of the VPD1. sources.bodyExcerpt: Boost Distortion – Tech 21 NYC Skip to content FIND A DEALER CONTACT US TECH 21 VIDEOS PRODUCT ARCHIVE NEWSLETTERS Facebook-f Instagram Youtube About Us Products Fly Rig Sansamp Effects & Midi Amplifiers Private Stock Accessories Hall of Fame Reviews Tech Notes Support About Us Products Fly Rig Sansamp Effects & Midi Amplifiers Private Stock Accessories Hall of Fame Reviews Tech Notes Support OWNER'S MANUAL BOOST DISTORTION DISTORTION, DIRT, GRIT, CHUNK, FUZZ, OVERDRIVE, GRIND... It goes by many names, comes in many flavors and they’re all good. Unfortunately, finding that sweet spot isn’t so easy with vintage pedals. You need to deal with noise, signal loss, tones that can change with battery life and even the temperature on stage. Some of those old Germanium-powered effects are more sensitive than a train-car of nitro. Tech 21’s all-analog circuitry squeezes righteous, vintage tones out of every Boost Series pedal with modern dependability. Designed and built from the ground up utilizing the best individually-selected, hand-biased discreet components, each unit delivers optimized performance with studio-quiet operation. And we call them Boost pedals for a reason. Alongside a wealth of hot driven tones, there is a powerful boost function that delivers up to an incredible 21dB of clean boost, which can be used independently from the effect. It is a true post-boost, punching up the tone you dialed in, not smothering it in unwanted distortion. From the high-impedance input to the sweepable low-pass filter in the tone control, your tone will be open and controllable in every setting. METALLIC SERIES New look, with same features and functionality. Hey, remember the ‘80s? A lot of bad clothes but some way-cool, aggressive distortions. Tight, muscular grind with buzz-saw harmonics never went out of fashion and the Boost Distortion delivers that fast punchy tone. It features its own unique SAG control that adds an expressive, tube-like response to every pick stroke. Operable with 9V alkaline battery (not included) or optional DC power supply (Tech 21 Model #DC4-A). Note: Videos shot using the original version. Unfortunately, finding that sweet spot isn’t so easy with vintage pedals. You need to deal with noise, signal loss, tones that can change with battery life and even the temperature on stage. Some of those old Germanium-powered effects are more sensitive than a train-car of nitro. Tech 21’s all-analog circuitry squeezes righteous, vintage tones out of every Boost Series pedal with modern dependability. Designed and built from the ground up utilizing the best individually-selected, hand-biased discreet components, each unit delivers optimized performance with studio-quiet operation. And we call them Boost pedals for a reason. Alongside a wealth of hot driven tones, there is a powerful boost function that delivers up to an incredible 21dB of clean boost, which can be used independently from the effect. It is a true post-boost, punching up the tone you dialed in, not smothering it in unwanted distortion. From the high-impedance input to the sweepable low-pass filter in the tone control, your tone will be open and controllable in every setting. Putting an overdrive pedal in front of a hard-pushed amp has been the secret weapon for generations of guitarists wanting to punch up the midrange and add sustain. The Boost Overdrive is packed with voluminous amounts of screamin’ tone. Just hit the Boost switch to go bigger and badder. The unique SPARKLE control adds upper harmonics for an open, snappy sound. • Operable with 9V alkaline battery (not included) or optional DC power supply ( Tech 21 Model #DC4-A). sources.bodyExcerpt: Double Drive – Tech 21 NYC Skip to content FIND A DEALER CONTACT US TECH 21 VIDEOS PRODUCT ARCHIVE NEWSLETTERS Facebook-f Instagram Youtube About Us Products Fly Rig Sansamp Effects & Midi Amplifiers Private Stock Accessories Hall of Fame Reviews Tech Notes Support About Us Products Fly Rig Sansamp Effects & Midi Amplifiers Private Stock Accessories Hall of Fame Reviews Tech Notes Support OWNER'S MANUAL DOUBLE DRIVE There is a good reason why many artists record and perform with several different amps running simultaneously. The best characteristics of each amp blend to create incredible and original tones. The Tech 21 Double Drive captures the lush, muscular power amp distortion of both Class A and Class A/B tube amps. Instead of just blending these tones, it feeds one into the other for massive ‘cascading’ distortion and limitless tonal variation. Sometimes more is more. CONTROLS INCLUDE DRIVE A controls the amount of Class A power amp output stage distortion (like Vox AC30®-style amp), rich in even harmonics. The amount of harmonics is dynamically controlled by the input level and their ratio by how hard you pick. DRIVE A/B controls the amount of Class A/B power amp output stage distortion (like Fender®/Marshall®-style amps), rich in odd harmonics. The signal path of Drive A runs into the signal path of Drive A/B. This results in an electronic multiplication, rather than addition, of the amount of distortion to achieve a cascading effect. sources.bodyExcerpt: Double Drive 3X – Tech 21 NYC Skip to content FIND A DEALER CONTACT US TECH 21 VIDEOS PRODUCT ARCHIVE NEWSLETTERS Facebook-f Instagram Youtube About Us Products Fly Rig Sansamp Effects & Midi Amplifiers Private Stock Accessories Hall of Fame Reviews Tech Notes Support About Us Products Fly Rig Sansamp Effects & Midi Amplifiers Private Stock Accessories Hall of Fame Reviews Tech Notes Support OWNER'S MANUAL DOUBLE DRIVE 3X This unique pedal design captures the lush, muscular power amp distortions of both Class A and Class A/B tube amps. The tones can be used individually or you can feed one into the other for massive ‘cascading’ distortion and limitless tonal variation. The 100% analog Double Drive 3X is a 3-channel, fully programmable version of its single channel predecessor and features active 3-band EQ. The expanded tone section gives you even greater flexibility to create incredible and original tones. You can store three custom sounds, even on the fly, by simply tweaking the knobs and double-tapping on a footswitch. How easy is that? And, with both Drives at minimum, you can program a clean boost up to 10dB for blazing solos. Sometimes more is more. Double Drive 3X MOD The Double Drive 3X has undergone a Private Stock MOD. It has been revoiced for more aggressive hard rock and metal tones rather than classic, bluesy-style tones. It features a tighter low end and a wider Level taper. The Double Drive 3X MOD is available at the same price as the original for a limited time. FEATURES • LEVEL is capable of extremely high output, up to 10dB (even in clean setting). Useful as a “pre-boost” for additional gain out of your amp without altering any tonal characteristics. • 1/4″ INPUT is 1megOhm high impedance input, same as traditional tube amps. • 1/4″ OUTPUT is 1kOhm low impedance output. • Can drive long cables without loss of signal integrity, even in bypass. • LED is highly efficient and low power consuming. It will fade as the battery runs low (±6.5V), although the Double Drive will continue to operate. • Utilizes standard 9V alkaline battery (not included) or optional power supply: Tech 21 Model #DC4-A. • Power Consumption: approx. 5mA. DRIVE A controls the amount of Class A power amp output stage distortion (like Vox AC30®-style amp), rich in even harmonics. The amount of harmonics is dynamically controlled by the input level and their ratio by how hard you pick. DRIVE A/B controls the amount of Class A/B power amp output stage distortion (like Fender®/Marshall®-style amps), rich in odd harmonics. The signal path of Drive A runs into the signal path of Drive A/B. This results in an electronic multiplication, rather than addition, of the amount of distortion to achieve a cascading effect. sources.description: Tech 21 Double Drive 3X is possibly the most unique pedal, offering analogue power amp drives at any volume. Check out my Tech 21 Double Drive 3X review here!
sources.snippet: Tech 21 Double Drive 3X - Analogue Power Amp Distortion
sources.bodyExcerpt: Tech 21 Double Drive 3X – Analogue Power Amp Distortion – cigilovic.com Skip to content cigilovic.com Music Gear and Equipment Reviews Articles Search for: cigilovic.com Music Gear and Equipment Reviews Articles Tech 21 Double Drive 3X – Analogue Power Amp Distortion Tech 21 Double Drive 3X is possibly the most unique pedal, offering analogue power amp drives at any volume. Check out my Tech 21 Double Drive 3X review here! Home Gear Reviews Tech 21 Double Drive 3X – Analogue Power Amp Distortion Share this post Share on Facebook Share on X (Twitter) Share on WhatsApp Share on Telegram Share on Reddit Share on E-mail Share on LinkedIn ★★★★★ ★★★★★ 4.5 / 5 Pros Possibly the most unique distortion pedal ever built Digitally savable three presets while retaining the analogue circuit Very easy to use, store and recall settings Cons Most settings generate a lot of compression More suitable on clean amps Feels like an experimental and unique pedal Where to buy Hello there, and welcome back to another cool guitar pedal review! This time, we will check out possibly the most unique Tech 21 pedals ever, the Tech 21 Double Drive 3X . As we always do, I will provide you with some background information on the Tech 21 NYC company as well as their legendary innovation, SansAmps . I have also prepared a sound demo for this Tech 21 Double Drive 3X review article to show you what Double Drive sounds like in combination with a tube amp (using reactive loads and IRs). Table of Contents About Tech 21 What is SansAmp? Tech 21 Double Drive 3X Using Double Drive Tech Specs Sound Demo (no talking) Review Pricing Availability Get notified of the new content (no spam!) You may have already encountered some of this blog’s content featuring Tech 21 products. The first time I started using Tech 21 products was way back in 2007, and it was my first ever proper guitar amp, Tech 21 Trademark 60 ! It was an excellent amp and a complete game-changer for a young guitar player with no gear experience! I also had the chance to borrow some other Tech 21 products, such as Tech 21 SansAmp PSA 1.1 and GT2 . A couple of years ago, I purchased their latest PSA, Tech 21 SansAmp PSA 2.0 and enjoyed it a lot! Check out my Tech 21 SansAmp PSA 2.0 review here Since I’d like to revisit their wonderful product line, I got myself a Tech 21 SansAmp TRI A.C. and wanted to give it a try after 15+ years! You may also check out my review and quick demo video if you are interested in one of the easiest-to-use SansAmp pedals ever! Check out my Tech 21 SansAmp TRI-A.C. review here Recently, I got the chance to collect some pedals during my visits to Türkiye and wanted to feature them here for you. Double Drive 3X was one of them, and I was really surprised with the results and how unique this pedal was. Unfortunately, this pedal was also discontinued a long time ago, but I believe people need to know about this wonderful design! Anyway, we will talk about the Double Drive 3X and hear how it sounds at the end of the article. Before we go into details, let’s have a look at the quick history of the Tech 21 NYC company . About Tech 21 B. Andrew Barta founded Tech 21 NYC in Midtown Manhattan in 1989 , unveiling his groundbreaking invention: the SansAmp. This innovative creation was born out of Andrew’s personal desire as a performing musician with an electronics background, whose day job involved repairing, modifying, and customising amplifiers. Armed with both technical expertise and unwavering determination, he brought his vision to life. Ironically, Andrew never set out to become a manufacturer. Initially, he sought to sell his technology to major companies, but they failed to recognise its potential or the transformative impact the SansAmp would later achieve. sources.description: A brief comparison and clarification of the seamingly similar Thorpy Bunker and Gunshot pedals
sources.snippet: ThorpyFX The Bunker vs ThorpyFX Gunshot - Guitar Pedal X
sources.bodyExcerpt: Guitar Pedal X - GPX Blog - ThorpyFX The Bunker vs ThorpyFX Gunshot ao link News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Xploration • Curation • Recommendation News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Filter content by area of interest Amps Boost and Overdrive Delay Distortion Fuzz Guitars Modulation Pitch Reverb Utility All All ThorpyFX The Bunker vs ThorpyFX Gunshot May 19, 2020 19:09 by Stefan Karlsson Boost and Overdrive Brown Sound Distortion Distortion Drive Effects Pedal Makers Marshall Style Distortion Overdrive ThorpyFX Versus + - Full Article Read Summary Key Points ThorpyFX's Gunshot (original) and The Bunker (Dan 'Lovetone' Coggins Brown Source MKII collaboration) share Thorpy's upper‑mids signature but are different circuits and enclosures: Gunshot polished steel; Bunker blackened anodised aluminium with silk‑screened graphics. Gunshot controls: Gain, Calibre, Tone, Volume; ranges from mellow to JCM800 saturation. The Bunker controls: Volume, Drive, Texture (more Texture when rolled back; dial up = more Brown Source), Mode (Top/Mid/Down), Tone; dual footswitches: On/Bypass and 'Sauce' tone‑stack bypass/boost. Tones: Gunshot warmer and rounded; Bunker brighter, tighter, punchier. They overlap and can be dialled similar; no clear winner. As of 2026-07-13, the price was £190. There’s been a lot of chatter online about the relative merits of the established Thorpy OG Gunshot Overdrive and its new The Bunker sort of challenger. I’ve always likened the Gunshot to a Hot Rodded Plexi - while Adrian has revealed that its profile is actually closer to that of a JCM800 - but obviously there are significant overlaps. By contrast, The Bunker is at its core much closer to a JTM45 / Plexi range with its Texture knob rolled back, while dialling up the Texture gives you a smoother, slightly more choked / compressed sound - more akin to the core Brown Source sound - which is intended to augment slightly cooking amps as such. There is very evidently some degree of shared territory here, while the pedals look and function quite differently - but if you really wish to you can dial them in to sound pretty similar. Both pedals have that distinctive upper mids frequency register which is one of the signature markers for a Thorpy circuit. I have both pedals so I thought I would run some comparisons - in terms of range covered, similarities and differences. The Bunker is obviously a Dan ’Lovetone’ Coggins collaboration which is identified by its blackened anodised aluminium plating vs the polished steel of the core Thorpy line. The graphics etc. on the Lovetone MKII pedals as such are also silk-screened, rather than laser-etched per the core Thorpy line - and the main font used is as per the original Lovetone pedals. The Bunker is very slightly dearer - by £5 at £190 - which is easily justified by its extra footswitch and Mode EQ Shift toggle-switch selector. As mentioned - the Gunshot is the OG ThorpyFX -

ThorpyFX - Electric Lightning - Overdrive quantity Add to cart SKU: LKPKO640220 Category: Effects - Overdrive Pedals 84 people are viewing this right now Estimated Delivery: Sep 30 - Oct 5 Free Shipping & Returns: On all orders Description Description From ThorpyFX : THE ELECTRIC LIGHTNING is a creation designed to meet the exacting needs of Chris Buck who utilizes a wide palette of sounds from crystal clear and punchy cleans through to nicely saturated overdrive. THE ELECTRIC LIGHTNING has two sides: a complex valve overdrive with 3 band Eq and a high headroom super clean boost on the right. The pedal is designed so that the boost runs into the valve overdrive side. This arrangement yields three distinct tonal variations ranging from clean boost all the way through to full and fat saturation. The pedal is designed to clean up impeccably from your volume control and as such it is ideal for dynamic players who like to constantly adjust their playing style. VOLUME: Use this control to increase the volume output of the drive side of pedal. GAIN: This control is used to increase the level of drive available on the drive side of the pedal, everything from lightly crispy through to heavier sounds is available here. BASS: This control gives allows you massive amounts of control over the bass response of the drive. Clockwise yields bass rich sounds. A little can go a long way, the EQ is powerful enough to cope with most backlines of varying EQ character. MIDS: This control gives allows you massive amounts of control over the mids response of the drive. Clockwise yields mids focused sounds. A little can go a long way, the EQ is powerful enough to cope with most backlines of varying EQ character. TREBLE: This control gives allows you massive amounts of control over the treble response of the drive. Clockwise yields treble focused sounds. A little can go a long way, the EQ is powerful enough to cope with most backlines of varying EQ character. BOOST: This control gives you control to boost or attenuate your signal, use it on its own as part of the boost side of the pedal or when stacked into the drive it can really make the pedal sing with complex harmonics and layered overdrive. LOWS: This control gives you control to add low end to the boost side of the pedal and fatten up your signal for crystal clear but fat clean sounds. LEFT FOOTSWITCH: This turns the drive side on/off. RIGHT FOOTSWITCH: This turns the boost side on/off. POWER: THE ELECTRIC LIGHTNING is designed to work at voltages of 12V DC. On power up, the inrush current can be as high as 700mA settling to 280-300mA during use. This should be provided from the supplied centre negative power supply. However, if your boards power supply can provide the requisite voltage and current requirements you can. Do not attempt to use this pedal with other voltages or polarities, the pedal can at best just not start up (limp mode) or at worst you can damage the sensitive internal electrics. Please be aware it takes a short period of time at first power up for the valve to heat to optimum level and begin working. COMPONENTS: To ensure consistency, reliability, low noise and tonal supremacy the ELECTRIC LIGHTNING is made with extremely high quality components. 1%

Their white-on-black graphics improve label legibility. All remaining pedals will gradually transition. Fallout Cloud retains the exact circuit and parts values. Camoflange uses a different BBD chip and improved power handling, stepping 9V to 24V, then 18V and optimal 15V; its bright, sparkly Vintage Electric Mistress style remains matched, with more headroom. As of the stated listing, the price was £199.99 for Fallout Cloud and £284.99 for Camoflange. The Thorpy Black Editions date back to 2020’s Lovetone / Dan Coggins evolved Field Marshal (Big Cheese) and The Bunker (Brown Source) pedals. Initially intended to mark them out as Lovetone derivatives, but which then gradually moved into the mainstream of the range. The Black Editions were very quick to find favour on account of their much improved label legibility - vs the etched steel originals. After the Field Marshal and The Bunker we had Black editions for the the Pulse Doppler Phaser (Lovetone Doppelgänger), ER-2 Uni-Vibe, The Dane MKII, Have Blue and Tacit Blue, Electric Lightning, and now Fallout Cloud and Camoflange. In fact all the remaining ones will be gradually brought across to the newer black edition facias - on a one-by-one basis. Some will be slightly re-calibrated, mostly owing to some slight parts changes. Thorpy tunes everything by ear, and very exactingly tests and refines each pedal over several iterations until they perfectly match their signature frequency curve. Sometimes even extending the range of coverage with a little more headroom and higher fidelity. Internally the Fallout Cloud is exactly the same circuit as it has been with all the same parts values. While for some pedals - including the Camoflange, some of those earlier parts have been fully expended, and the circuit has needed to be re-calibrated with a slightly different supporting array of components. Login here 0 Cart Your cart is empty Shop our products Electric Guitars Acoustic Guitars Amplifiers Effects & Pedals Accessories Contact Us Home All products ThorpyFx Hanami Fuzz Roll over image to zoom in Click on image to zoom / ThorpyFx Hanami Fuzz Save $-399.00 ThorpyFX Price: Sale price $399.00 / Quantity: Add to cart Share this product Description HANAMI is a fuzz we feel is a natural successor sonically from where the BONEYARD left off. Rather than seeking to emulate anyone else’s circuits, HANAMI sits perfectly between the BONEYARD and the FALLOUT CLOUD. It is a fuzz that takes inspiration from the past but offers modern features and a sonic footprint that is inspirational no matter what styles of music you play. Built with 4x NOS germanium transistors and 1x NOS Germanium Diode. HANAMI is loaded with saturation offering smooth, rewarding and evolutionary fuzz tones from one easy to navigate control set. VOLUME: Use this control to balance the output of the pedal. Unity (where the volume out matches the volume in) is roughly at the 10 o’clock position, depending on your guitars pickup output. BOOST: This control allows you to adjust the pedals character from smooth lower gain fuzz through to a more saturated aggressive and smile inducing fuzz. TREBLE: This control adds or cuts Treble to the Fuzz. Fully counter clockwise removes treble and fully clockwise boosts treble. This control is very interactive with the bass control. BASS: This control adds or cuts Bass to the Fuzz. Fully counter clockwise removes Bass and fully clockwise boosts Bass. This control is very interactive with the Treble control. Adjusting the Bass and Treble control allows you to tailor the tonality of the fuzz to match your guitar and amp. POWER: HANAMI is designed to work at voltages of 9V DC. This can be from a quality centre negative power supply such as the Gigrig Generator or Voodoo Lab Pedalpower Plus 2. Do not attempt to use this pedal with other voltages or polarities. sources.snippet: ThorpyFX Judge Dredd Lawbringer (Gunshot)
sources.bodyExcerpt: ThorpyFX Judge Dredd Lawbringer (Gunshot) | Axe... And You Shall Receive Skip to main content Boutique Vintage Guitar Effects, Guitars Amplifiers 🇺🇸 USD 🇨🇦 CAD 0 items Menu Search Search Main navigation Catalog Home Brands What's Hot Search Search Store info News About Contact ThorpyFX Judge Dredd Lawbringer (Gunshot) Brand: ThorpyFX $309.00 Body "I AM THE LAW" ThorpyFx X 2000AD Collaboration The Lawbringer overdrive aims to place Law above all else in line with Judge Dredds singular uncompromising attitude. with stacked gain stages you can blend the calibre and gain together to tailor and deliver the perfect British style overdrive. The Lawbringer is based upon The award winning Gunshot overdrive. Designed to deliver awesome rock tones you love, with refreshed artwork. The Lawbringer/GUNSHOT was designed to be the overdrive to beat all others. Sonically most overdrives can sound thin or lack a certain “something” when compared to a real valve amplifier. It’s an unfair comparison really, but it is possible to solve this problem. This is where the Lawbringer/GUNSHOT comes in, at the heart of the pedal is a proprietary cascading "gain engine" tuned to deliver maximum tonality for as wide a range of amps as possible. Through tweaking the pedals controls to taste you can achieve overdrive flavours from subtle through to searing, think slightly hairy blues to hard rock. The tones produced are addictive and inspiring in equal measure. ThorpyFx The Peacekeeper quantity Add to cart Description From Thorpy: The PEACEKEEPERis our take on a low gain overdrive designed to suit all guitars and all amps whilst delivering the sweetest on the edge to crunch tones you have ever heard. Hyperbole aside, this pedal has somevery cunning tricks up its sleeve, by combining a post gain active Treble and Bass circuit with a pre-gain Mids/presence control you are able to tailor the overdrive character and tonality to your exacting needs. The pre-gain mids control allows you to move from a very smooth mid scooped gain type to a more pronounced mid humped gain with all the subtleties in between. Post gain the active treble and bass controls adapt that focussed gain stage to achieve the tonality you desire/need. Used as a subtle boost into your amp (ala Klon style) or as an “on the Edge” overdrive, the PEACEKEEPERwill make you wonder how you sound so good! Learn more Featured Deal Save $100 on an exclusive Olive Green Line 6 HX Stomp Claim Reviews The Big Review: ThorpyFX Scarlet Tunic – A secret portal to early Pink Floyd tones and more This tone-shaping preamp promises assorted flavours of interstellar overdrive… but does the world really need a Selmer in a box? by Richard Purvis August 04, 2022 by Richard Purvis August 04, 2022 When you purchase through affiliate links on Guitar.com, you may contribute to our site through commissions. Learn more Review Overview Our rating 8 Our verdict A vintage-voiced preamp that covers a range of tones, but with the emphasis very much on shimmery scuzz. They say the Selmer company still makes a mean saxophone. These days you don’t hear so much about the long-defunct amplifier brand that started out as a London-based offshoot of that French firm, but there was a time when it seemed destined to be the sound of the British rock boom. READ MORE: Chapman ML3 Semi-Hollow Pro review: A hard-charging wolf in spangly sheep’s clothing What went wrong? Well, the biggie was that the Beatles , the Shadows and the Animals all jumped ship to Vox ; but one player who was still using his Selmer towards the end of the 60s was Pink Floyd’s original frontman, Syd Barrett … and that brings us to the ThorpyFX Scarlet Tunic. You may be wondering why ThorpyFX, one of the UK’s most respected indie pedal builders, decided to create an ‘analogue emulator’ of Syd’s Selmer Treble ’N’ Bass 50 head. It actually started out as a favour for Lee Harris, the guitarist in Nick Mason’s Saucerful Of Secrets – basically a tribute act to Barrett-era Floyd, except with the real band’s drummer. For Harris, the appeal of having a TNB50 in a box is obvious: it enables him to recreate those early Floyd tones without having to take a rare, heavy and potentially unreliable 50-Watt head on tour. For the rest of us, it’s not so clear – after all, the amp in question is in the same ballpark as an EL34-driven Marshall JTM45 and there are already plenty of pedals that do that job. Maybe this is a chance for us to re-evaluate Selmer’s place in amplifier history. There’s no doubting the TNB50 is a killer amp, especially in its mid-60s ‘croc-skin’ iteration, and there has been talk of a Selmer revival in recent years (Alex Turner of the Arctic Monkeys is a big fan of the Zodiac Twin 30 combo). That said, this is not purely a one-amp emulator. Adrian Thorpe is keen to point out that it can also cover the sounds of the Vox AC30 and Hiwatt DR103 – the latter being, perhaps not entirely coincidentally, strongly associated with the man who replaced Barrett in Pink Floyd, David Gilmour . So while the Scarlet Tunic doesn’t have the separate treble and bass channels of the original Selmer amp, it does have a presence control for adjusting the upper-midrange response. You also get – alongside output volume, gain, bass and treble knobs – a trio of three-way toggle switches. These let you play with the character of the bass and treble, and set the input sensitivity. As ever with Thorpy, it’s a forbidding chunk of heavy metal with the controls protected by perforated side-walls painted in a feature colour. In this case that’s red, naturally, but it’s actually more crimson than scarlet. We’re pretty sure Syd wouldn’t mind. In use One thing you just have to get used to with ThorpyFX pedals is that the controls are not easy to read. Everything is etched into polished steel, and if the light’s falling at the wrong angle you’d be better off with Braille. That said, the arrangement of the five knobs is intuitive enough and easy to learn. Your reviewer has owned a few Selmers down the years, inc

Login here 0 Cart Your cart is empty Shop our products Electric Guitars Acoustic Guitars Amplifiers Effects & Pedals Accessories Contact Us Home All products ThorpyFX Six Zero Roll over image to zoom in Click on image to zoom / ThorpyFX Six Zero Save $-299.00 ThorpyFX Price: Sale price $299.00 / Quantity: Add to cart Share this product Description The SIX ZERO was designed to look back to the 1960s and forward to the 2024s and imagine what a new pedal could look and sound like now whilst operating with a fundamentally vintage sound at its core. To capture this decade spanning sound we chose to recreate the sounds of the venerable MKI TB. As fuzz enthusiasts will know, the MKI Tonebender was designed with germanium transistors, and it sounded incredible. But germanium was replaced for a reason (not thermally stable, finicky, inconsistent) so we decided to make the fuzz side silicon, but tuned it to sound and respond as if it were germanium. We then coupled this incredible fuzz with a modified version of the discrete tremolo circuit designed by Dan Coggins way back when he first started designing guitar effect circuits. With controls for Depth, Rate, Attack and Level this purely analog pedal keeps it functionally simple whilst being deceptively feature packed. This pedal allows you to deliver an almost unlimited tonal pallet no matter what your mood/style or guitar and amp setup. DEPTH: This control allows you to mix how much tremolo you want in with your dry signal. RATE: This controls the rate of the tremolo, from super slow to super-fast. If turning when playing, the effect will “duck” out of the way before returning at the new speed. ATTACK: This control isn’t necessarily a typical gain control, there is a sweet spot on the attack where the fuzz sounds the richest, with the right amount of sustain, clarity, and harmonic content without becoming overly harsh or too smooth. Outside of the sweet spot you can find many textures and different character from gated and spitty to smooth and liquid. LEVEL: This control dictates how loud the fuzz is, we have put plenty of volume into the pedal, please be aware that too much level can overwhelm the tremolo. Use with care!! LEFT FOOTSWITCH: This turns the tremolo on/off. RIGHT FOOTSWITCH: This turns the fuzz side on/off. POWER: The SIX ZERO is designed to work at voltages of 9V DC and draws a maximum of 35mA current. This should be from a quality center negative power supply such as the CIOKS DC7. Do not attempt to use this pedal with other voltages or polarit

sources.h1: Lazy J x ThorpyFX The J review: “one of the best sounding, most tactile and responsive dirt pedals I’ve ever played”
sources.description: The Lazy J x ThorpyFX The J promises to put classic vintage amp tones in your rig for a fraction of the price
sources.snippet: Lazy J x ThorpyFX The J review: a superb tweed amp emulation | Guitar.com
sources.bodyExcerpt: Lazy J x ThorpyFX The J review: a superb tweed amp emulation | Guitar.com News Reviews Guides Features Magazine Tuner Deals Related Brands Lazy J ThorpyFX Related Tags # Effects # Overdrive # Pedals When you purchase through affiliate links on Guitar.com, you may contribute to our site through commissions. Learn more Featured Deal Sterling By Music Man Sabre – save a massive $500 on this dent and scratch model at Sweetwater Claim Reviews Lazy J x ThorpyFX The J review: “one of the best sounding, most tactile and responsive dirt pedals I’ve ever played” Have you ever felt the need for Tweed but not the cash to splash? This collab from two UK boutique heavyweights promises to put classic vintage amp tones in your rig for a fraction of the price Lazy J x ThorpyFX The J. Image: Press by Ed Oleszko January 14, 2026 by Ed Oleszko January 14, 2026 When you purchase through affiliate links on Guitar.com, you may contribute to our site through commissions. Learn more Review Overview Our rating 10 Our verdict ⊕ Boutique Tweed tones in a box ⊕ More versatile than you’d imagine ⊕ Incredibly responsive and good purely as a drive pedal ⊖ A real valve version would be a nice extension of the format The J crucially captures not only the ‘Tweed Tone’ perfectly but crucially the feel and response of plugging into a real Tweed Lazy J20 amp. One of the most organic, touch sensitive and responsive overdrive pedals around £329 / $399, thorpyfx.com Collabs are all the rage in the pedal world these days, but it’s still exciting when you see someone enter the field that hasn’t been there before. Jesse Hoff, the main man behind Lazy J , has won a reputation as one of the world’s foremost boutique amp makers over the last few decades. You’ll find his takes on vintage Tweed amps on stages and in studios with everyone from David Gilmour and Noel Gallagher to Ed O’Brien and Joe Satriani . READ MORE: Horrothia Effects Triage Deluxe review – the ultimate all-in-one gain machine for fussy tonehounds? Hoff is also no stranger to effects either, having put out the well-regarded Cruiser boost/drive pedal well over a decade ago. But collaborations? That’s a new one. Thorpy main man Adrian Thorpe is much more familiar with that sort of thing of course – whether that’s making signature gear for Chris Buck and Danish Pete , or collaborating with pedal legend Dan Coggins to revive both the Dinosaural and Lovetone brands. Two tone connoisseurs teaming up to make something altogether a bit different for both of them then? Well, that sounds like a lot of fun… “I like to work with good people who genuinely inspire me,” Thorpe tells me. “Jesse is such a great guy, one of the great amp builders. I’ve been an owner and huge fan of his Lazy J J 20 amp for years. It’s such a harmonically rich and beautifully tactile amp to play. It’s taken us about four years of collaboration to develop The J pedal, and we’re really proud of the result.” Image: Press Lazy J x Thorpy Fx The J – what is it? As Adrian implies, the primary mission of The J is to faithfully emulate the tones and response of a J 20 amp in compact pedal format, itself derived from the classic Fender 5E3 Tweed Deluxe amp. To do that, The J includes a built-in transformer that can mimic the real amp feel, paired with a circuit chock full of high-grade audiophile capacitors and such. All of it is built to Thorpy’s famously military-grade specs, and differs from the usual Thorpy fare by squeezing it all into a rather lovely UV-printed enclosure. It’s still recognisably a Thorpy pedal of course, but one that feels equally indebted to the Lazy J boutique amp lineage. As with the original, you get the option of a normal or bright channel, and the controls are suitably spartan for an amp based on the similarly simple J 20 – with independent volume for each, as well as a presence control, single tone and a master output. Things you won’t find on the top of the J 20 include a toggle switch to select X

sources.bodyExcerpt: Thorpy FX The J – Coast Sonic Skip to content Search Home Shop Hi-Fives News Contact Account Search Cart Home Shop Hi-Fives News Contact Home Thorpy FX The J Skip to product information Previous Next Previous Next Close Thorpy FX The J Regular price $399.00 USD More stock coming soon By Thorpy FX Quantity Add to cart Maker: Thorpy FX Model: The J Condition: New Description: THE J is the second pedal in our “Analog amp emulator” series. This concept aims to capture what you hear from an amplifiers. I’ve been friends with Jesse Hoff for years, several years ago I cheekily suggested I’d like to capture what his flagship Lazy J the “J20” sounds and feels like. To my delight Jesse agreed, and we began working our magic together. In the pedal development we made sure that the enhanced chewy tweed tones of the J20 were covered tonally but as always, we went further than the initial scope of design. Fitted with a high-quality transformer, the pedal reacts to your playing and overdrives and feels like a full-size amplifier. THE ”J” as an Analog amp emulator can work fantastically well with your existing amp, your existing pedals and it integrates easily into your current rig. You can use it to create beautiful, enhanced tweed “LAZY J - J20” vintage amp sounds or craft your own sound. Tested worldwide during its development on the biggest of stages, you can be confident the “J” will deliver. CONTROLS: LEFT FOOTSWITCH: ON/OFF. Turns the pedal on and off, true bypass. RIGHT FOOTSWITCH: Switches between the Normal and Bright Channel. OUTPUT: This is the Master Volume and controls overall output. RESPONSE: A subtle presence adjustment control. SUPPLY: Emulates the Voltage attenuation control in the J20- Full clockwise is full voltage, anything below this emulates voltage attenuation. NORMAL: Controls the volume/gain for the normal channel. TONE: This allows you to dial in the EQ you’d like for the pedal, from dark to strident. BRIGHT: Controls the Volume/Gain for the Bright channel. X / Y SWITCH: This allows you to select what emulated input valve you want, 12AX7 for medium gain tones and 12AY7 for lower gain drive. POWER: THE J is designed to be powered by a 9V DC centre-negative 2.1mm power supply. Internally the voltage is bumped up to 18V. Do not attempt to use this pedal with other voltages or polarities. We have power protection circuitry in our pedals and use of any other voltages will shut the pedal down and require return to ThorpyFx HQ for repair. This will not be covered under warranty. sources.description: Adrian does ‘rocky’ with an American flavour.

sources.bodyExcerpt: ThorpyFX Warthog review | Guitar.com News Reviews Guides Features Magazine Tuner Deals Related Brands ThorpyFX Related Tags # Distortion # Effects When you purchase through affiliate links on Guitar.com, you may contribute to our site through commissions. Learn more Featured Deal UAFX Flow – save £101 Claim Reviews ThorpyFX Warthog review Adrian does ‘rocky’ with an American flavour. by Chris Vinnicombe May 11, 2016 by Chris Vinnicombe May 11, 2016 When you purchase through affiliate links on Guitar.com, you may contribute to our site through commissions. Learn more F ollowing last month’s in-depth look at British Army Major Adrian Thorpe’s Peacekeeper low-gainer, here we turn our attention to a very different animal from the same stable as 2015’s Gunshot, an award winner in these very pages. Where the Peacekeeper is all about boosting and augmenting your core tone, the Warthog (war and peace… geddit?) is designed to bring the filth. Thorpe explains: “The Warthog was designed at the same time as the Gunshot. I wanted it to complement the Gunshot, and consequently it has a flatter, less mid-focused EQ – and it can get cleaner and much dirtier, too; at the far reaches of the calibre and gain knobs it is fuzzy in its breakup. If I had to sum up the Warthog, I’d say its distortion characteristics were American in flavour – eg, a driven tweed amp through to higher gain.” In common with the other ThorpyFX pedals we’ve tested, construction standards are very high; the Neutrik jack sockets and true-bypass footswitch – rated at many thousands of cycles – are off-board to maximise road-worthiness, while WIMA and Panasonic capacitors, a Burr Brown op amp and metal film resistors with a one per cent tolerance give the internals a premium vibe. Externally, Thorpy’s now-familiar laser-etched stainless steel enclosure is paired with a ‘faded sonic blue’ powder-coated base plate and red mini chickenhead knobs. It looks great and our only quibble is that the mirror-like stainless steel makes the control panel lettering hard to read from a standing position under stage lights. Still, it doesn’t take long to learn what each of the four knobs does. Aside from gain and volume, the tone control rolls off high end as you turn it up, and the calibre brings a ‘secret sauce’ of saturation, grit and heat to the table. In use Anyone with a fondness for 1990s American alternative rock will love the Warthog. Imagine a great Rat pedal that occupies the space between overdrive and fuzz, minus the over-compressed response that often stops a Rat cutting through live. With the calibre and gain cranked, the Warthog delivers a joyful brand of carnage; a kind of fuzz-meets-distortion that’s almost Muff-like in its saturation to the extent that you can pull off Siamese Dream -era Smashing Pumpkins riffs and solos but, crucially, you won’t disappear in the mix or experience a total meltdown. Back off the calibre control and the voicing is more amp-like, albeit a 6L6 or 6V6-loaded amp working hard. Roll the calibre clockwise again, but this time tame the gain to find Nirvana and early Foo Fighters tones. We wish this pedal had existed in 1994 because, unlike the DS-1 (too quiet), Rat (too compressed) and Big Muff (disappears in a band) pedals on countless garage floors in the mid-90s, the Warthog has the headroom, punch and grit to give your sound a sufficiently aggressive kick. And it sounds great. Oh to be 15 again… Key features ThorpyFX Warthog •  Price £185 •  Description True-bypass overdrive/distortion pedal powered by 9v centre-negative power supply or battery, made in UK •  Controls Gain, tone, volume, calibre •  Dimensions 70mm(w)x145mm(d)x60mm(h) •  Contact thorpyfx.com Chris Vinnicombe Former Guitar.com Chief Editor Chris Vinnicombe has spent the past two decades playing the world’s greatest guitars and interviewing legendary guitarists and key industry figures. Through minute tailoring of the circuit, the WARTHOG delivers the biggest range of tones of any overdrive/distortion pedal on the market. With an ability to go from crystal clean boost through todistortion the WARTHOG has sonic characteristics that match the military prowess of its namesake. Its tonality is firmly in the American camp with sparkling cleans similar to the best amplifiers in that genre, With the calibre and gain controls cranked you get a crushing distortion with fuzzy overtones at the very extremes of travel. All settings are extremely addictive, with a 3 dimensional and complex sound that makes your playing jump from the fretboard. Aside from achieving fantastic sonic credentials the WARTHOGis built like a tank with physical features such as recessed knobs and top mounted jacks. Robust build does not have to come at the sacrifice of looks, the WARTHOG uses a combination of a beautiful stainless steel laser etched centre console wrapped in a tough powder coated baseplate. Internally the pedal is immaculately built using premium 1% metalfilm resistors, Wima and Panasonic capacitors, Neutrik jacks and a Burr-Brown Opamp. Theseare the crme de la crme of the electronics world and when coupled with a robust gold plated PCB and dust sealed potentiometers the recipe is as good as it can possibly be. sources.bodyExcerpt: GOLDEN PLEXI- Plexi Style Distortion-TONE CITY ▏Analog Pedals & Power supplies PRODUCTS MINI Overdrive Nashiville Sweet Cream Bad Horse Mandragora Blues Man Noble Man Dry Martini Kaffir Lime Distortion/Fuzz London Bender Golden Plexi Wild Fire Matcha Cream Fuxx Fuzz Black Tea Mickey Delay/Reverb/Chorus Tape Machine Angel Wing Tiny Spring Phaser/Tremelo Summer orange Tremble Compressor/Boost Buzz Bee Comp Engine All Spark DELUXE Heavenly Lake-Reverb&Delay King of Blues-Overdrive Model M-Distortion Holy Aura-Distortion Big Rumble-Overdrive CUSTOM Durple - Overdrive Wildfro-Distortion Lilheat-Overdrive Double Durple-OD&Boost TPS TPS-5 TPS-6 TPS-8 TPS-10 TPS-12 POWER STICK LEGEND Green Tube Blue Crystal Golden Face ULTIMATE 龍 LOONG ARTISTS COMMUNITY YouTube Instagram Facebook SUPPORT Certification TEST & REPORT E-CATALOGUE E-MANUAL DISTRIBUTOR ABOUT US CONTACT CN EN HOME - PRODUCTS - MINI GOLDEN PLEXI- Plexi Style Distortion Input Impendence: 500K Output Impendence:10K Current Draw: 15 mA Power Supply: DC 9V adapter DM.: 9.4(L)*4.5(W)*4.8(H) (cm) N.W.: 0.27kg True Bypass Product Description Gear Demos Related Gear Manual & Report Where to buy Golden Plexi is a classic rock amp sound with a timeless plexi-style tone lifted from the very best legendary black and gold amplifiers. In 2022, we refined the gain structure of the Golden Plexi to provide a more focused and consistent high-gain dynamic response, renaming it the Golden Plexi2. While this version received excellent feedback, we also heard many requests for the return of the original Golden Plexi—with its wider adjustable high-gain range.Realizing that we should not let people miss out on this amazing"mini-pedal miracle," the original version Golden Plexi is back for the 2025 version, and it renamed as name: Golden Plexi. An added toggle switch allows users to switch the tone from a right side tightened gain ( Golden Plexi 2) to left side more high gain and bass (low gain). This version also optimizes the high frequencies in TONE. It's actually very quiet. While there are only four controls on this mini pedal, we has incorporated the essentials. The volume control acts as you would normally expect, with the tone and gain control shaving a wider range than you would expect. Delivering everything from a sweet crunch to crushing high-gain, this versatile pedal lets you attain fantastic tones suitable for blues, rock and metal. The sensitivity of the tone control means that you can run this pedal into the clean channel of nearly any amplifier and get the classic plexi sound you are craving. Keep the control low for a smooth lead tone, or crank it higher for a more cutting sound that'll pierce through nicely in a mix. This is an mini wonders that worth your trying.
